card.text: The hottest planet, hidden beneath thick clouds.

introduction.text: Venus is the second planet from the Sun. It spins backward, and one day there lasts longer than its year.

clouds.title: Venus’s clouds
clouds.summary: Thick clouds hide Venus’s ground. This is an illustration, not a photograph.

radar.title: Radar map of the ground
radar.summary: Magellan’s radar mapped the ground beneath the clouds. The orange color is added, not measured.

elevation.title: Height of the solid surface
elevation.summary: Radar measurements reveal Venus’s plains and mountains beneath the clouds; colors show height above a reference sphere.

ultraviolet.title: Akatsuki ultraviolet photograph
ultraviolet.summary: Venus in ultraviolet light from orbit on 30 August 2023. Gray marks the half the camera could not see.

emissivity.title: How efficiently the surface emits
emissivity.summary: Warm ground gives off microwaves; emissivity measures how efficiently it does so compared with an ideal emitter.

reflectivity.title: How strongly the surface reflects
reflectivity.summary: Magellan sent radar through the clouds; this map estimates how reflective the ground is at that wavelength.

roughness.title: Small-scale bumps seen by radar
roughness.summary: Radar echoes reveal how uneven the ground is at scales of meters; larger values mean a rougher surface.

gravity.title: Gravity anomaly
gravity.summary: Radio tracking of Magellan measured where Venus pulls a little harder or weaker than a smooth planet.

gravity-uncertainty.title: How well gravity is known
gravity-uncertainty.summary: The one-sigma uncertainty of the gravity map; larger where Magellan flew high.

bouguer.title: Gravity without the topography
bouguer.summary: Gravity after subtracting the pull of the visible mountains and lowlands, which points to mass below them.

geoid.title: Shape of Venus’s gravity
geoid.summary: The height of the surface of equal gravity potential, the level a global ocean would settle to.
